title: Lubinsky wants to record Grimes without Parker
summary: Herman Lubinsky offered a date for the quartet without Parker, Grimes insisted on him, and Ross Russell objected to Grimes singing.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: and here he comes and say "Man I want to record you" But it didn't cost nothin' much to record. I think the scale was 44 dollars.
Q He heard you with Parker?

Well, no he had heard me before. 'Cause he had been coming to see me the whole time. But this particular time Parker was there, and he had only been there a few days, but he was playing, you know what I mean. And when I got through playing, Lubinsky approached me and said "I got a little date for you if you want it". I said, "yeah, great." He say, "Just the four of you" I said, "well, no, I got this saxophone player." He say, "yeah I heard him, but like I don't understand what he doin'. So, you don't need him. I give you the date if you want." So I just held out. I said, so I said "The man been playin with me and [he] may be some thin' new. You go and we use the horn whether you like it or not. Maybe somebody else might like it." That's exactly how I talked to him. And we had a ring-a-round the rosey thing goin for a while, and he said, "well alright meet me the next day," and the next day I met him at the place called the White Rose I think... Right around the corner where everybody went. A little bar, right on 6th Avenue that everybody

hung out. It was a hang out place. Everybody hung out there during the intermission. Nice bartender named Johnny, and it was a nice place, so I met him there and we had this controversy again about the saxophone player, Charlie Parker. So he finally agreed. I said, 'oh, man, it'll be all right.' And so we made the date. When we got down there he wanted me to sing, B--Tanning from the singing-- this guy gave me a hard time cause I sang a time. what the hell business is it if I get to sing, and when I did sing I let Parker take all the playing. I did the singing and where I should have been playing I let him play. The first eight bars, as you might say... And the guy still give me a hard time, what was his name?
And he made a big to-do out of that that I shouldn't have been singing, I should have let Parker play more. I'm the one that cause of him being on in the first place
Lubinsky was the one that hired me...
